result.title: Definition Grounding in Theory-Level Auto-formalization
result.summary: LLM-based auto-formalization systems can now generate formally verified Lean code at unprecedented rates. However, a formalization advances mathematical research only when further mathematical results can be built on it, especially when its definitions and helper lemmas are general enough to be imported and used idiomatically. We propose definition grounding, where definition formalizations are continuously judged and revised, as a method to ensure formalization quality. We find that agents formalizing definitions from textbook text often produce definitions that later statements cannot use, and only 25%-50% of their definition sets are compatible with all later statements. However, clarifying the informal definitions can improve this rate up to 77.5% averaged over all models. Furthermore, stating a small set of basic properties without proving them can improve model judges' capability to detect definitions with compatibility issues, at only about 11% of the definition formalization cost. These results are verified with ReuseBench, a benchmark we curated for formalizing new mathematical fields and theories.

AI.brief_summary: 论文提出「definition grounding」，在 LLM 自动形式化（Lean）中持续评判与修正定义，并构建 ReuseBench 基准衡量定义能否被后续命题复用：原始定义兼容率仅 25%–50%，澄清非形式定义后平均升至 77.5%，仅陈述少量未证明的基本性质即可用约 11% 成本提升模型判别兼容问题的能力。
AI.relevance_reason: 定义能否被后续命题复用的评判—修正流程，可能为 LVR 中 latent 状态是否仍可被后续推理步骤使用的检测提供借鉴线索；其低成本「陈述性质」式判别信号能否用于发现不可用的内部表示，可供核查。
